```yaml
name: Gemini Code Review

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Set up Ruby
      uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: '3.0'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        gem install gemini-ai-client

    - name: Run Gemini Code Review
      env:
        GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
      run: |
        gemini-ai-client --model gemini-2.5-flash --input-file .github/workflows/review-template.md --output-file .github/workflows/review-output.md

    - name: Upload review as comment
      uses: actions/github-script@v4
      with:
        github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        script: |
          const fs = require('fs');
          const content = fs.readFileSync('.github/workflows/review-output.md', 'utf8');
          await github.rest.issues.createComment({
            owner: context.repo.owner,
            repo: context.repo.repo,
            issue_number: context.issue.number,
            body: content
          });
```

This GitHub Actions workflow sets up a job named "review" that triggers on pull requests to the `main` branch. It checks out the code, sets up Ruby, installs the `gemini-ai-client`, runs the Gemini Code Review using the `gemini-2.5-flash` model, and uploads the review output as a comment on the pull request. The `GEMINI_API_KEY` secret is required to authenticate with the Gemini API.
